criterion: On the letter every paragraph appears once in the ordinary document flow and once again inside a layer the scroll drives.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each paragraph of the letter is present twice in the delivered markup, once in normal flow and once inside an inert scroll-driven layer. Answer no when only one copy of a paragraph exists, or when the scroll-driven copy is the only copy present.

criterion: On the letter a faint speckle overlay sits above the film and below the darkening panel.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a faint animated speckle covers the film stage, sits above the film and its still frame, and sits below the darkening panel. Answer no when the speckle is absent, or when it sits above the darkening panel, or when it obscures the writing.

criterion: The shop offers its five products in one editorial order as its only arrangement.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the catalogue presents the products in a fixed editorial order with neither a search field nor a filter control on the page. Answer no when a search field, a filter control or a sort control appears, or when the order follows price or name.

criterion: On a product page in the shop the specifications appear as a table whose figures align down a column.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a product page renders its specifications as a labelled table with the numeric column aligned. Answer no when the specifications appear as running prose, or when the figures sit ragged against one another.

criterion: On the cart the quantity control edits a line in place and the totals show a pending state until the server answers.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when changing a quantity on the cart updates the number at once, marks the totals as pending, and reverts the number with a stated reason when the server rejects the change. Answer no when the page reloads to change a quantity, or when a rejected change leaves the wrong number in place.

criterion: On a product page in the shop a discontinued product shows a support note naming the date support ends.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a discontinued product renders a note stating that the product is no longer sold together with the date support runs until. Answer no when the discontinued product renders as an ordinary available product, or when the note omits the date.

criterion: On the firmware installer a device capability that is absent produces an explanation in place of any control.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the installer, in a browser lacking the device capability, renders a full explanation naming the browsers that work and offers the in-application path with no connect control shown. Answer no when a connect control is rendered that cannot function, or when the page renders empty.

criterion: On the cart an estimate note sits above the totals until the delivery address is known.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the cart labels its shipping and tax figures as estimates and carries a sentence saying the exact amount follows the address. Answer no when the cart presents shipping and tax as final before an address is entered.

criterion: On the account camera grid an expired warranty appears as a neutral state.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a camera whose warranty has ended is marked in the same neutral treatment as ordinary information. Answer no when an expired warranty is marked as a warning or an error.

criterion: Every surface after the letter reads as dense and free of ornament.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the shop, the cart, the account and the download page present tightly set information with no decorative imagery or oversized hero composition. Answer no when any of those surfaces carries a marketing hero, a decorative illustration or generous editorial whitespace.

criterion: The letter sits on a dark ground, and the shop, the cart and the account sit on a light ground.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the letter and its footer render light type on a dark ground and the commerce and account surfaces render dark type on a light ground. Answer no when any of those surfaces uses the other ground.

criterion: One accent colour appears at most once on any screen of the shop, the cart, the account or the letter.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a single saturated accent hue appears at most once per screen and is used as type or as a mark rather than as a background behind text. Answer no when the accent appears more than once on one screen, or when text sits on the accent.

criterion: Across the shop, the cart and the account every transition moves at one speed and reads as a machine responding.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when hover, focus, press and disclosure changes across those surfaces share one short linear timing with no overshoot or bounce. Answer no when different controls move at visibly different speeds, or when any control eases with a spring.

criterion: Across the shop and the account a state change is stated in words before any colour carries the meaning.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a success, a failure and an in-progress state each carry a written label beside whatever colour marks them. Answer no when any of those states is signalled by colour or by movement alone.

criterion: On a narrow viewport the left rail collapses to one control at the top of the content column.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the persistent rail on the shop, the cart and the account becomes a single control above the content on a narrow viewport and returns to a rail on a wide one. Answer no when the rail stays a rail at every width, or when it disappears with no replacement.

criterion: On the cart a notice about a changed price disappears on its own.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a notice about a price or availability change on the cart fades away or dismisses itself without the reader acting. Answer no when that notice stays in place until the reader resolves it. Yes records a defect.

criterion: The letter carries a price, a form or a navigation element beyond its wordmark and its footer.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the letter shows a price, a form field or a navigation element other than the wordmark and the footer row. Answer no when the letter carries only its title, its dateline, its paragraphs, its closing line and the footer. Yes records a defect.

criterion: The source contains no module for a staff console, a returns workflow, a jobs listing or a legal document library, none of which the brief asks for.
evaluation_rule: A module is a route, a page component, an API handler or a database table in the delivered source, not a word in copy. The routes this brief asks for are the letter, the shop and its product pages, the cart, the three checkout steps, an order by token, the downloads archive, the doctor installer, sign-in, sign-up and the account routes. Yes if every route, handler and table in the source serves one of those. No if the source carries a staff or admin console route, a returns or RMA workflow, a careers or jobs listing, or a legal document library of terms and privacy pages, or any table backing one of those.

criterion: The source declares no client library for a second datastore, an object store, a cache, a queue or a third party mail vendor in its dependency manifest.
evaluation_rule: A dependency is a package named in the runtime dependency block of the app's package manifest, not a transitive lock entry and not a development-only tool. Yes if every runtime dependency is Astro, Hono, a PostgreSQL driver, an SMTP mail client, an HTTP client used to reach killbill, a password hash, or a direct requirement of one of those. No if the manifest names a second datastore client such as a MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB or Redis driver, an object-store client, a queue client, a cache client, or a third party mail vendor SDK such as SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark or Resend.

criterion: The source keeps the scroll driver, the cart controls, the firmware installer and the serial register row as the only client-side modules, with every other route built as server-rendered markup.
evaluation_rule: A client-side module is a component hydrated with a client directive or otherwise shipped to the browser as a mounted framework component, not an inline script that only wires up a form. Yes if the only hydrated islands are the front page scroll driver, the cart quantity controls, the doctor firmware installer and the register row on the cameras page, and every other route is server-rendered markup complete on first paint. No if the catalogue, a product page, a checkout step, the downloads archive or an account list is hydrated as a client component, or if the whole app is mounted as one client-side root.

criterion: The source carries no analytics client, no consent module and no outbound tracking beacon.
evaluation_rule: An outbound tracking beacon is a request the delivered pages make to a host other than this app's own origin, killbill at PAYMENTS_API_URL or the Mailpit SMTP host. Yes if the source declares no analytics package, no consent or cookie-notice module, and no such beacon. No if the source loads an analytics or session-replay script such as Google Analytics, Plausible, Segment, PostHog or Sentry, declares a consent banner component, or posts page views or events to an external endpoint.

criterion: Money is represented as an integer count of minor units in every module that touches it, with no float arithmetic and no currency parsing from formatted strings.
evaluation_rule: Money is any usd figure this app stores, computes or renders -- a variant price, a cart line unit price, an order subtotal, shipping, tax, discount and the order total. Yes if every one of those is carried as an integer count of minor units in every layer including the browser island code, and a decimal appears only where a figure is formatted for display or sent to killbill as the invoice amount. No if a schema column or a field declares money as a float, real, double or decimal type, if a price is divided into a float to be added or taxed, if tax is taken with a floating point rate rather than integer arithmetic truncated toward zero, or if a figure is parsed back out of a formatted string such as "$415.80".

criterion: One shared helper resolves the acting customer for every account-scoped query, rather than each handler repeating its own ownership filter.
evaluation_rule: An account-scoped query is any read or write restricted to the signed-in customer -- their orders, their cameras, their ownership rows, their account page. Yes if one shared helper or middleware resolves the acting customer from the bearer token and every account-scoped handler obtains the customer identity through it. No if two or more handlers each decode the token themselves, or each write their own customer_id filter inline, so that a new handler could be added with the filter forgotten and nothing in the source would catch it.

criterion: One seeding routine owns the catalogue, the devices, the releases and the firmware images, and is written so a second run inserts nothing.
evaluation_rule: Seeding is the code that inserts the fixture rows the brief pins -- the two customers, the five catalogue products with their variants and inventory, the shipment protection rungs, the four devices, the four Arranger releases and the four firmware entries. Yes if a single seeding routine owns all of that and every insert is written so a second run adds no row, through an upsert, a conflict clause on the unique key or an existence check. No if seed rows are written from more than one place, such as a migration and a separate seed script both inserting products, or if any insert would duplicate a row on restart because it carries no conflict handling.

criterion: Every host, port and credential the app needs is read through one configuration module that reads the environment, with no literal host or port elsewhere in the source.
evaluation_rule: Configuration is every host, port, URL and credential the app needs -- DATABASE_URL, SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, PAYMENTS_API_URL, PAYMENTS_API_KEY, PAYMENTS_API_SECRET, PAYMENTS_APP_USER and PAYMENTS_APP_PASSWORD. Yes if one configuration module reads the environment for all of them and every other module takes its values from that module. No if a handler, a database client or a mail client reads the environment directly for one of those values outside that module, or if a literal host, port or credential -- localhost, 127.0.0.1, a bare 5432 or 8080, an SMTP password -- appears in application code anywhere but that module's own defaults.

criterion: The four release note groups are declared once as an ordered constant and referenced from every module that reads or writes them.
evaluation_rule: The four release note groups are Newly Added, Improvements, Bug Fixes and Known Issues, in that fixed order and with none invented beyond them. Yes if those four labels and their order are declared once as a single ordered constant and every module that reads or writes notes -- the seed, the downloads archive, the per-version route -- references that constant. No if the labels are spelled out again in a second module, if the seed and the renderer each carry their own copy of the ordering, or if a fifth group name appears anywhere in the source.
